title: Web export: tab freezes (OOM in audio worklet) ~5-8s after a long AudioStream starts playing
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible: v4.6.stable [89cea1439], v4.7.stable [5b4e0cb0f]
- Earlier versions not tested.

### System information

Web export, Compatibility renderer, no-threads build. Reproduced in current Chrome and Edge on Windows and Linux (AudioCont ext at 48000 Hz).

### Issue description

Playing a ~60 s music track through a plain `AudioStreamPlayer` in a web
export freezes the whole browser tab a consistent 5-8 seconds after
playback starts: rendering and input stop permanently while already-
buffered audio keeps playing briefly (in Sample mode the decoded looping
buffer plays on indefinitely). DevTools, if opened beforehand, pauses
"before potential out-of-memory crash" with the stack in the audio
worklet message pump (`index.audio.worklet.js`, `node.port.onmessage` /
`heapSlice`).

Ruled out by testing each variable in isolation (all still freeze):

- codec — ogg vorbis, mp3, and uncompressed WAV/PCM all freeze (so not decode cost)
- `default_playback_type.web` — both Stream and Sample
- channels / rate — mono and stereo, 22.05-44.1 kHz content
- mix rate — freezes with `audio/driver/mix_rate.web=0` (mixer confirmed at the context's 48 kHz)
- engine version — identical on 4.6 and 4.7

Not affected: short SFX one-shots and a continuously running
`AudioStreamGenerator` are stable indefinitely; builds where the music
never plays are stable. Playing the same files through a plain JS
`Audio()` element instead is stable (our current workaround).

Possibly related: #115560 (web OOB, 4.6 regression, audio-labeled —
closest), #106098 (sample-type web memory leak), #104645, #109728;
historical: #96068.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Web export (no threads, Compatibility) with a ~60 s ogg/mp3/wav played
   via `AudioStreamPlayer` (loop on).
2. Open in Chrome or Edge, click once (autoplay unlock), let it play.
3. Tab freezes within ~5-8 s.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Can extract an MRP on request — the trigger is exactly the steps above
with any ~60 s track.
